es.summary: Acumulación de líquido en la cavidad peritoneal, generalmente secundaria a cirrosis y hipertensión portal.
key_points: Se asocia a hipertensión portal y bajo nivel de albúmina.
El gradiente sérico‑ascítico (SAAG) >1.1 g/dL indica origen portal.
El manejo incluye restricción de sodio y diuréticos espironolactona + furosemida.

pathophysiology: Cirrrosis → fibrosis hepática → aumento de resistencia al flujo portal.
Hipertensión portal eleva la presión hidrostática capilar peritoneal.
Hipoproteinemia disminuye la presión oncótica plasmática.
Se produce filtración de líquido al espacio peritoneal (transudado).
risk_factors: Cirrhosis por alcohol o hepatitis viral.
Síndrome nefrótico o pérdida de albúmina.
signs_symptoms: Distensión abdominal visible y sensación de plenitud.
diagnostics: Examen físico: onda de fluido y signo de shifting dullness.
Ecografía abdominal: líquido libre en cavidad peritoneal.
treatment: Diuréticos: espironolactona + furosemida (típico esquema 100 mg/40 mg).
Paracentesis terapéutica cuando >5 L o disnea severa.
Infusión de albúmina 25 g/2 L de suero tras paracentesis >5 L.
nursing_care: Medir circunferencia abdominal y peso diario.
Monitorear presión arterial, frecuencia cardíaca y saturación.
Registrar ingesta y eliminación; vigilar I&O.
Controlar electrolitos y función renal cada 24‑48 h.
patient_teaching: Dieta baja en sodio: evitar alimentos procesados y sal añadida.
Pesarse cada mañana y reportar aumentos >0.5 kg en 2 días.
Tomar diuréticos según indicación y no suspender sin autorización.
Reconocer signos de infección: fiebre, dolor abdominal, cambios en el líquido.
Acudir al servicio de salud si hay sangrado de varices o dificultad respiratoria.

outcomes: Circunferencia abdominal disminuye ≥2 cm en 5 días

interventions.action: Evaluar peso y circunferencia abdominal cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar cambios en el volumen de líquido rápidamente.

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y eliminación, enfatizando I&O estricto
interventions.rationale: Facilita el cálculo de balance hídrico.

interventions.action: Administrar diuréticos según prescripción y observar respuesta
interventions.rationale: Promueve la eliminación de exceso de sodio y agua.

interventions.action: Enseñar dieta baja en sodio (<2 g/día) y revisar lista de alimentos
interventions.rationale: Reduce la retención de líquido.

interventions.action: Posicionar al paciente en semi‑Fowler y cambiar posición cada 2 h
interventions.rationale: Mejora la expansión pulmonar y reduce la presión intraabdominal.

outcomes: Sin fiebre ni dolor abdominal durante 7 días
Cultivo de líquido ascítico negativo en controles

interventions.action: Mantener técnica aséptica estricta al realizar paracentesis
interventions.rationale: Previene la introducción de microorganismos al líquido peritoneal.

interventions.action: Monitorear temperatura y signos de infección cada 8 h
interventions.rationale: Detección temprana de peritonitis bacteriana espontánea.

interventions.action: Evaluar el aspecto y olor del líquido ascítico al drenarse
interventions.rationale: Cambios pueden indicar contaminación o infección.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre signos de infección y cuándo buscar ayuda
interventions.rationale: Facilita la intervención oportuna.

interventions.action: Administrar profilaxis antibiótica si está indicada por el médico
interventions.rationale: Reduce la incidencia de peritonitis en pacientes de alto riesgo.

en.summary: Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity, usually secondary to cirrhosis and portal hypertension.
key_points: Associated with portal hypertension and low albumin level.
Serum‑ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) >1.1 g/dL indicates portal origin.
Management includes sodium restriction and diuretics spironolactone + furosemide.

pathophysiology: Cirrhosis → hepatic fibrosis → increased resistance to portal flow.
Portal hypertension raises peritoneal capillary hydrostatic pressure.
Fluid filters into the peritoneal space (transudate).
signs_symptoms: Visible abdominal distension and fullness sensation.
diagnostics: Physical exam: fluid wave and shifting dullness sign.
Abdominal ultrasound: free fluid in peritoneal cavity.
Labs: low albumin, elevated INR, altered electrolytes.
treatment: Therapeutic paracentesis when >5 L or severe dyspnea.
Albumin infusion 25 g/2 L of saline after paracentesis >5 L.
nursing_care: Measure abdominal circumference and daily weight.
Monitor blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation.
Record intake and output; watch I&O.
Check electrolytes and renal function every 24‑48 h.
patient_teaching: Low‑sodium diet: avoid processed foods and added salt.
Weigh each morning and report increases >0.5 kg in 2 days.
Take diuretics as prescribed and do not stop without permission.
Recognize infection signs: fever, abdominal pain, fluid changes.
Seek medical care if variceal bleeding or breathing difficulty occurs.

outcomes: Abdominal circumference decreases ≥2 cm in 5 days

interventions.action: Assess weight and abdominal circumference every 24 h
interventions.rationale: Detects fluid volume changes quickly.

interventions.action: Record intake and output with strict I&O
interventions.rationale: Facilitates fluid balance calculation.

interventions.action: Administer diuretics per prescription and observe response
interventions.rationale: Promotes excess sodium and water elimination.

interventions.action: Teach low‑sodium diet (<2 g/day) and review food list
interventions.rationale: Reduces fluid retention.

interventions.action: Position patient semi‑Fowler and change position every 2 h
interventions.rationale: Improves lung expansion and reduces intraabdominal pressure.

outcomes: No fever or abdominal pain for 7 days
Negative ascitic fluid culture on follow‑up

interventions.action: Maintain strict aseptic technique during paracentesis
interventions.rationale: Prevents introduction of microorganisms into peritoneal fluid.

interventions.action: Monitor temperature and infection signs every 8 h
interventions.rationale: Early detection of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

interventions.action: Evaluate appearance and odor of ascitic fluid when drained
interventions.rationale: Changes may indicate contamination or infection.

interventions.action: Educate patient on infection signs and when to seek help
interventions.rationale: Facilitates timely intervention.

interventions.action: Administer antibiotic prophylaxis if indicated by physician
interventions.rationale: Reduces incidence of peritonitis in high‑risk patients.

sources.name: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Hepatic and Biliary Disorders

summary.0.quote: Ascites is an accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity ( Figure 19.19 ) that is caused by cirrhosis of the liver.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Portal Hypertension Another liver condition, portal hypertension , is an increase in pressure within the portal venous system because of resistance to portal blood flow.

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: Ascites is a condition in which the abdominal cavity fills with fluid that shifts from the intravascular to the interstitial space, resulting in hypovolemia.

sections.treatment.4.quote: Treatment Identify and treat the underlying cause.

sections.complications.1.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.complications.2.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: These include administering medications documenting daily weights and abdominal girth measurement educating patients monitoring laboratory values, such as sodium levels monitoring vital signs and intake and output

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: On the inpatient side, the patient will be admitted to the ICU and will have vital signs recorded a minimum of every hour, as well as intake and output data.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: A sodium-restricted diet will help control fluid retention.
